assessment: Two nondemented levodopa-responsive parkinsonism autopsy cases with Alzheimer-type neuropathology; no sage exposure or facial-expression comparison in abstract. Original scanned body inaccessible through attempted PMC and publisher PDF routes; this exclusion is restricted to abstract context.

Clinical review of Parkinson sexual dysfunction and therapeutic approaches, published by SAGE; body discusses sexual expression and treatments, with no ground Salvia intervention or facial expressiveness outcome comparison.

Three former boxers with dementia pugilistica versus three autopsy controls in biochemical brain tissue assays; SAGE is publisher, not ingestion of sage, and no facial-expression dietary intervention is reported.

Differential diagnosis describes one Parkinson case and two essential tremor cases, with facial hypomimia among clinical signs; no sage exposure. PMC8848065 is a duplicate presentation of the same 2013 case series, not another study.

Case of Parkinson and schizophrenia with clozapine-associated neutropenia managed with G-CSF; examination records hypomimia, and discussion notes passage hallucinations. Neither sage exposure nor food comparison appears.
Same 2013 essential tremor versus Parkinson three-case presentation as PMID23700378, assigned another PMC and DOI; facial hypomimia diagnostic discussion without sage food exposure.

Observational study 90 Parkinson patients and 52 controls evaluates leg weakness; MDS-UPDRS-III facial-expression item appears in subgroup tables, but no ground sage assigned or intake contrasted. SAGE is publisher.
Globular glial tauopathy clinicopathology case describes marked hypomimia; Sage Therapeutics appears as a disclosure/funder name, not Salvia consumption or facial response to food.

Descriptive Parkinson questionnaire study predicts depression and discusses overlap with hypomimia; no sage ingestion or manipulation. The Geriatric Depression Scale is an assessment, not an herb preparation.

LRRK2 G2019S clinicopathological cases assess Parkinson symptoms and Lewy body pathology; no ground-sage diet intervention or exposure-specific facial endpoint. SAGE-type lexical hits do not establish plant ingestion.
Ischemic-stroke vascular parkinsonism case reports hypomimia and levodopa trial, without ground-sage exposure or comparison; publisher is SAGE.
Five post-anoxic parkinsonism cases treated with dopaminergic drugs include hypomimia on clinical examination; no sage ingestion or botanical effect was tested.

Twenty-eight Parkinson patients, relatives and observer compare home diary motor-state ratings; hypomimia is among manifestations explained during training. No sage food intervention or dietary measurement.

1984 letter on exercise-provoked foot dystonia describes a runner with facial hypomimia and additional cases; original p.885 via scanned BMJ-hosted copy. No sage exposure. OCR interleaves adjacent letters; use only named letter column.

Materials use commercial mushroom-derived tyrosinase in levodopa microneedle biosensor; species is not identified as shiitake and enzyme is not consumed. Parkinson participants ingest prescribed carbidopa/levodopa, with rest tremor included in modified motor score; healthy volunteers separately eat cooked fava beans, not shiitake.
126 probable Alzheimer outpatients and 29 controls; hypomimia reported at 60% in patient group. Sage is publisher, not an administered herb; no ground sage comparison. Full PDF not reviewed.
Retrospective movement clinic series of 36 psychogenic parkinsonism patients; none had hypomimia. Jacob I Sage is first author; no culinary sage exposure or food comparison. Full text not obtained.

Rotenone PD-model mice: control and two enriched mixtures contained 0.9, 0.1 and 0.2 g coconut oil per 100 g chow; rotarod time improved in enriched mixtures but multiple other ingredients changed. Coconut refining not specified; apparatus latency differs from human fall frequency.

Six SOD1 ALS mice per group received extra virgin coconut oil mixed with chow versus standard chow; grid-hang paw grip latency to fall improved on weeks 14–16. It was extra virgin, not refined; apparatus endurance is not spontaneous fall frequency, and the model is not Parkinson disease.

MPTP mice fed mixed MCT ketogenic versus control chow, both containing coconut oil (381 vs 20 g in diet table); multiple macronutrients differed. Rotarod latency improved for MPTP/MCT diet versus MPTP/control; no isolated coconut, confirmed refining or clinical falls.

Review lists lentils among acetylcholine food sources and glutamic-acid-containing legumes; neither boiled-lentil intervention nor insomnia comparison is reported. Ingredient-to-neurotransmitter hypothesis is not measured clinical effect.
General review describes resting tremor as a PD feature and proposes mushroom-derived ergothioneine as research direction; no cooked shiitake administered or tremor comparison.

Review of erinacine-enriched Hericium erinaceus lion's mane mycelia; discusses MPTP rodent rotarod and baseline PD tremor. Different species and preparation; no cooked shiitake human resting-tremor comparison.
Review describes resting tremor in PD and generic mushrooms as a source of niacin; cites rodent nicotinamide studies, not cooked shiitake or a food/tremor comparison.

Vitamin D review describes resting tremor in PD and lists ultraviolet-exposed mushrooms as a source, without shiitake-specific cooked exposure or a tremor outcome contrast. Local source dated 2025-12-16.
